fine_trace.code: const auto first = Data[0] & 0x0F; const unsigned int second = (Data[0] & 0xF0) >> 4;
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled first byte selects the argument type (low nibble) and the argument-name length (high nibble).
argsize is validated to be in (0, Size) so the argument name and format string are non-empty.
The format string is copied into a separately allocated, tightly sized buffer of exactly Size bytes, making any out-of-bounds read detectable by ASAN.
The format string view has no NUL terminator; its end pointer is exactly one past the last byte of the buffer.
The format string is parsed by fmt::format_to, entering parse_format_string and then parse_replacement_field.
The named argument id is parsed; the format spec parsing then proceeds with begin pointing at the ':' character.
parse_align is called with begin pointing at the first byte of the fill/alignment spec, and end pointing one past the last byte of the tightly sized format buffer.
next_code_point is called with begin pointing at a multi-byte UTF-8 lead byte (e.g. 0xE0) whose continuation bytes extend to the very end of the buffer.
The lead byte has the high bit set, so the function enters the do-while loop to skip continuation bytes.

The loop advances through continuation bytes. When begin reaches the last byte of the buffer and that byte is a continuation byte, ++begin makes begin == end; the short-circuit condition begin != end prevents reading *end, so the loop exits and returns end.
When next_code_point returns end (because the multi-byte char extends to the buffer end), p is reset to begin, so the loop reads *p = *begin which is the last valid byte.
The loop reads *p. If the last byte is an align character (e.g. '>'), align is set and p != begin, so handler.on_fill is called with a fill length of p - begin.
The fill string_view spans from begin to p. When p points to the last byte, begin = p + 1 = end, which is a valid one-past-end pointer.
After parse_align, begin may equal end, and parse_format_specs returns end. The subsequent parse_replacement_field checks *begin != '}' and reports 'missing }'.

fine_trace.code: if (begin == end || *begin != '}') return handler.on_error("unknown format specifier"), end;
fine_trace.note: When begin == end, the check short-circuits and no out-of-bounds read occurs here. The vulnerability manifests as a stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 when the multi-byte fill char's continuation bytes extend exactly to the end of the tightly allocated format buffer, causing next_code_point to read one byte past the buffer in the do-while condition when the last byte is a continuation byte and begin is one past the last byte.
